newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Autoliv sees merger complete March/April.
newsitem.headline: Autoliv sees merger complete March/April.

text.p: A merger between car safety equipment maker Autoliv and the automotive component unit of U.S. Morton International Inc could be finalised in March or April, a company spokesman said on Thursday.
"We are awaiting U.S. tax authorities' decision which we think we will receive at the end of March or the beginning of April," Autoliv spokesman Mats Odman told Reuters.
The merger, first mooted in September, will create one of the world's largest airbag operations, called Autoliv Inc.
Odman said the merger had both income and cost advantages.

"Through the merger we will more than double our market share in the world on ready made airbags from 12 to 25 percent. Morton's strong position in the U.S. and Japan complements us well," Odman said.
"In addition we will receive access to gas components that Morton manufactures which we buy today."
Autoliv is also considering more acquisitions in the future, Odman said.

"We are always interested in changes that move our market position forward. If there are other companies that satisfy our requirements and that are for sale or are interested in cooperation, we are not disinterested," he said.
He also said there would be fewer companies in the sector in the future.

"There are too many companies in the sector. In Sweden there once were three to five seatbelt makers earlier but now there are only four in the whole world. Today there are eight airbag manufactures in Europe alone.
"The development will be the same in this branch and there will be fewer companies," he said.
